chunks: 3955 - The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, passed by the hoarders and ordered that their hoarded goods be brought out into the open parts of the markets and where people could see them. Then it was said to the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, “If only you would fix prices for them.” So he, peace be upon him, became angry until anger was recognized in his face, and he said: “Am I to fix prices for them? Indeed, pricing belongs to Allah, Mighty and Majestic; He raises it when He wills and lowers it when He wills.”

key_terms.السِّعْرُ: the price or market rate of goods
key_terms.الْمُحْتَكِرِينَ: those who hoard goods to restrict supply and harm buyers
key_terms.بُطُونِ الْأَسْوَاقِ: the open central areas of the marketplaces
key_terms.حُكْرَتِهِمْ: their hoarded stock kept back from the market
key_terms.قَوَّمْتَ: you fixed or set a price

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about hoarding goods and fixing market prices in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله ordering hoarded goods to be exposed in the marketplace so that people could access them openly. When asked to impose pricing, he rejected this and affirmed that price fluctuation ultimately lies with Allah عَزَّ وَجَلَّ. The report relates to the prohibition of hoarding and the limits of market intervention.
